nodes.description: Solve real-world and mathematical problems by writing and solving equations of the form x + p = q and px = q for cases in which p, q and x are all nonnegative rational numbers .
nodes.label: 6.EE.B.7

nodes.description: Add and subtract fractions with unlike denominators (including mixed numbers) by replacing given fractions with equivalent fractions in such a way as to produce an equivalent sum or difference of fractions with like denominators. For example, 2/3 + 5/4 = 8/12 + 15/12 = 23/12. (In general, a/b + c/d = (ad + bc)/bd.)
nodes.label: 5.NF.A.1

nodes.description: Interpret and compute quotients of fractions , and solve word problems involving division of fractions by fractions, e.g., by using visual fraction models and equations to represent the problem. For example, create a story context for (2/3) ÷ (3/4) and use a visual fraction model to show the quotient; use the relationship between multiplication and division to explain that (2/3) ÷ (3/4) = 8/9 because 3/4 of 8/9 is 2/3. (In general, (a/b) ÷ (c/d) = ad/bc.) How much chocolate will each person get if 3 people share 1/2 lb of chocolate equally? How many 3/4-cup servings are in 2/3 of a cup of yogurt? How wide is a rectangular strip of land with length 3/4 mi and area 1/2 square mi?
nodes.label: 6.NS.A.1

nodes.description: Apply and extend previous understandings of multiplication to multiply a fraction or whole number by a fraction.
nodes.label: 5.NF.B.4

nodes.description: Understand signs of numbers in ordered pairs as indicating locations in quadrants of the coordinate plane; recognize that when two ordered pairs differ only by signs, the locations of the points are related by reflections across one or both axes.
nodes.label: 6.NS.C.6b

nodes.description: Use a pair of perpendicular number lines, called axes, to define a coordinate system, with the intersection of the lines (the origin) arranged to coincide with the 0 on each line and a given point in the plane located by using an ordered pair of numbers, called its coordinates. Understand that the first number indicates how far to travel from the origin in the direction of one axis, and the second number indicates how far to travel in the direction of the second axis, with the convention that the names of the two axes and the coordinates correspond (e.g., x-axis and x-coordinate, y-axis and y-coordinate).

set.reason: Reading a root from an x-intercept and checking it by substitution needs equation-solution meaning, not the broader transposition/like-term procedure. Gemini confuses the algebraic alternative with the graphical criterion; propose the concept endpoint separately.
set.scope: relating kx+b=0 solution to graph

set.reason: The graphical criterion interprets the intercept abscissa as the value satisfying the equation; this concept is necessary while the original transposition procedure is optional. Root checked both endpoint-based reviews; each identifies the stated content or conditional method rather than a curriculum-order claim.
set.scope: The meaning of an equation solution when identifying it with a graph intercept

set.reason: The stated correspondence reads an equation root as the x-coordinate of the graph's x-intercept.
set.scope: reading equation solution as x-intercept

set.reason: Decimal addition/subtraction helps solve and check equations with decimal constants. The source places no integer-only restriction, so Gemini's integer example disproves necessity without disproving this useful preparation; integer equations avoid the decimal algorithm.
set.scope: equations with decimal coefficients or constants

set.reason: A factor and a multiple are defined through a product a×b=c. Finding factor pairs and listing multiples both presuppose understanding what a multiplication equation states.
